guide.title: Medication Administration Skills
guide.lead: The hands-on part of pharmacology: confirm the indication, check the contraindications, give it by the right technique, then watch what it does. Write it down as soon as it's given.

sections.title: Technique by route
rows: Under the tongue, mouth closed, don't swallow; sitting or lying
Aspirin chewed; glucose gel between cheek and gum – only if alert and swallowing
Outer mid-thigh, through clothing if needed; hold as the device instructs; massage the site
Atomiser, half in each nostril, about 1 mL per side at most
6–8 L/min oxygen or air; mask or mouthpiece; can run in-line with CPAP or bag-mask
Spacer, shake, one puff, slow deep breaths

sections.title: Before you give
rows: SBP below 90 mmHg (or 30 below baseline), HR below 50 or above 100, RV infarction, PDE-5 inhibitor (24 hours sildenafil or vardenafil, 48 hours tadalafil)
Can't swallow or protect the airway
Reduced consciousness, caustics, hydrocarbons; only with medical direction

rows.dose: 0.3 mg IM; 0.15 mg if under 25 kg

sections.title: Record
items: Drug, dose, route, site, time, who gave it
Vital signs and symptoms before and after
Side effects; who authorised it (medical direction if required)

quiz.q: Before nitroglycerin, the patient says he took sildenafil 12 hours ago. You:
options: Withhold nitroglycerin and tell medical direction and the hospital
Give and monitor BP every 2 minutes
quiz.explanation: Sildenafil within 24 hours; tadalafil within 48 hours.

quiz.q: Unresponsive hypoglycaemic patient (42 mg/dL) who can't swallow. Next?
options: No oral glucose; IM glucagon or IV dextrose per protocol
Glucose gel in the cheek anyway
0.15 mg IM (junior auto-injector) into the outer thigh

quiz.q: After aspirin 324 mg for chest pain, most important follow-up?
options: Document time, dose and response, and reassess
Under the tongue, mouth closed, not swallowed
quiz.explanation: Have the patient sit or lie.

options: An alert patient after a recent pill ingestion

quiz.q: Naloxone for a 14 kg toddler (oxycodone, RR 6):
Nitroglycerin is withheld if the heart rate is:
Using a metered-dose inhaler in an emergency:
options: With a spacer, one puff at a time, slow deep breaths

flashcards.question: Six rights
flashcards.answer: Right patient, medication, dose, route, time, documentation.

flashcards.question: Three label checks
flashcards.answer: When taking it out, when preparing, before giving.

flashcards.question: Epinephrine auto-injector
flashcards.answer: Outer mid-thigh IM. Adult 0.3 mg; under 25 kg 0.15 mg.

flashcards.question: Nitroglycerin contraindications
flashcards.answer: SBP below 90 mmHg (or 30 below baseline), HR below 50 or above 100, RV infarction, PDE-5 inhibitor within 24 hours (sildenafil, vardenafil) or 48 hours (tadalafil).

flashcards.question: Activated charcoal contraindications
flashcards.answer: Reduced consciousness or unprotected airway, caustics, hydrocarbons. Only with medical direction.

flashcards.question: Common EMS routes
flashcards.answer: Oral, buccal, sublingual, IM, intranasal, inhaled (and IV/IO at advanced levels).

flashcards.question: Pediatric doses
flashcards.answer: Weight-based; length-based tape for weight and equipment; have a partner check every pediatric dose.

flashcards.question: Documenting a drug
flashcards.answer: Time, drug, dose, route, site, response before and after, side effects, who authorised it.

critical.scenario: Crushing chest pain, SBP 92, HR 104; took tadalafil 36 hours ago. Your partner wants to give nitroglycerin because it's 'clearly an MI'.
critical.question: Correct action?

options.t: Withhold nitroglycerin (tadalafil within 48 hours and borderline BP); aspirin chewed, 12-lead, oxygen to target, transport

critical.explanation: Tell the hospital about the tadalafil.
critical.kpi: Identifies PDE-5 inhibitor contraindication to nitroglycerin

critical.scenario: 3-year-old (14 kg) with an empty oxycodone bottle nearby: lethargic, RR 6, SpO₂ 82%. You have naloxone 2 mg/2 mL, an atomiser and syringes.
critical.question: Dose and technique?

options.t: Bag-mask with oxygen first; naloxone 0.1 mg/kg = 1.4 mg (1.4 mL), split between nostrils; reassess; transport and watch for re-sedation

options.f: Use the weight-based dose you can titrate.

critical.scenario: COPD flare: RR 28, SpO₂ 85%, wheeze. She offers her own nebuliser and albuterol vials.
critical.question: Correct sequence?

options.t: Oxygen titrated to 88–92%, check her vials' drug and concentration, give nebulised albuterol with your equipment per protocol, reassess

critical.explanation: Add ipratropium if your protocol allows.
critical.kpi: Administers nebulised bronchodilator safely in COPD
